title: Methods Development for Blood Borne Macrophage Carriage of Nanoformulated Antiretroviral Drugs
protocol: Weigh the drug crystals and various surfactants for nanoformulations using an analytical balance.
Mix the weighed materials with 10 mM Hepes buffer, pH 7.8 using a T-18 Ultraturrax mixer until completely dispersed.
Load 50 mL of beads into the grinding chamber using a funnel.
Ensure the O-ring is in place on the milling chamber.
Select an appropriate screen mesh size for continuous milling.
Secure the lids by tightening the nuts.
Make sure that the product outlet tube empties into the collecting vessel.
Add the drug suspension with various amounts of surfactants to the product inlet ensuring a minimum volume of 100 mL.
Start the pump using the control unit at a flow rate between 50 - 150 mL/min as required for your formulation.
Turn the agitator on and adjust the speed on the control unit from 620 rpm to 4320 rpm as needed.
Monitor the temperature in the grinding chamber using the attached gauge to ensure no overheating occurs.
Mill the sample at various speeds and flow rates, taking out small aliquots (~1 mL) for size and charge measurements using a Diffraction Light Scattering Brookhaven Zetasizer.
Stop the milling when the desired particle size is achieved using the control unit.
With the pump still running, collect the sample into a flask to allow complete drainage of the drug.
Switch off the pump after draining.
Place a collection tray under the unit and loosen the nuts on the front plate of the lid assembly to remove the beads.
Collect the beads in the tray and take off the front plate.
Use a deionized water bottle to wash the beads into the tray.
Transfer the milled suspension into 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Set the centrifuge to 10,000 rpm (10,174 rcf) for 30 minutes.
Measure the amount of supernatant after centrifugation.
Replace the supernatant with an equal volume of fresh surfactant solution.
Transfer the resuspended material back into the milling chamber.
Mill the suspension for 10 minutes.
Take an aliquot (~1 mL) and measure size and charge using the Zetasizer.
Clean the MicroCer equipment post-use with deionized water.
Clean the MicroCer equipment with 70% ethanol after water cleaning.
Measure the concentration of nanoART formulations using HPLC.
Prepare samples for reversed phase HPLC analysis using triplicate 20 μL injections.
Inject samples onto a YMC Octyl C8 column with a C8 guard cartridge.
Pump mobile phase consisting of 48% acetonitrile and 52% 25 mM KH2PO4, pH 4.15 at 0.4 mL/min.
Detect UV/Vis spectra of samples at 272 nm for quantitation.
Compare sample measurements to a standard curve prepared from free drug in methanol (concentrations ranging from 0.025-100 μg/mL).
Measure the drug crystals and various surfactants using an analytical balance.
Mix measured amounts with 10 mM Hepes buffer, pH 7.8 for dispersion.
Disperse the mixture completely using a T-18 Ultraturrax mixer.
Transfer the suspension to the homogenizing vessel.
Begin recirculation.
Ensure the chiller is on before starting to homogenize the sample.
Gradually increase pressure until the meter reads 20,000 ± 2,000 psi.
Continue to homogenize until the target particle size is achieved.
Take an aliquot (~1 mL) periodically and measure the size and charge of the sample using a Zetasizer.
Transfer the homogenized suspension from the homogenizer to 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Set the centrifuge to 10,000 rpm (10,174 rcf) for 30 minutes.
Measure the amount of supernatant after completion of the centrifuge cycle.
Replace the measured volume of supernatant with an equal volume of fresh surfactant solution.
Transfer the suspension to the C5 homogenizer after resuspension.
Restart circulation and return the homogenizing pressure to 20,000 ± 2,000 psi.
Homogenize for 30 minutes.
Measure the size and charge of the formulation using the Zetasizer.
Perform post cleaning of the unit with deionized water and ethanol as the solvent.
Measure the concentration of the samples using HPLC.
Measure 50 mL of dichloromethane into a glass beaker.
Measure 6 g of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) using an analytical balance, add to the dichloromethane.
Mix until complete dissolution is observed.
Measure 1.25 g of drug crystals and add to dichloromethane/PLGA solution.
Mix until complete dissolution is achieved.
Make a 1% polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) surfactant solution and cool it using an ice bath.
Pour the dissolved drug solution into the cooled PVA surfactant solution.
Start the ultrasonicator at 50% amplitude.
Sonicate the sample for 10 minutes.
Take out a small aliquot (~1 mL) for particle size analysis.
If particle size is greater than 1.5 μm, sonicate the sample in 2-minute intervals up to a maximum of 16 minutes total.
Observe the samples under microscope at 20x and document observations.
Use a stir plate to create an adequate vortex for the remaining suspension.
Continue mixing overnight at room temperature.
Weigh 8 g mannitol into a flask.
Add 80 mL RO water to the flask.
Mix until complete dissolution is observed.
Store the solution at room temperature.
Collect the suspension after 24 hours.
Pour the suspension into 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the samples at 8,000 rpm for 20 minutes at 5°C.
Decant the supernatant from the samples.
Resuspend one half of the sample in 75 mL filtered RO water.
Resuspend the other half in 75 mL 0.5% CTAB surfactant.
Centrifuge the samples again at 8,000 rpm for 20 minutes at 5°C.
Resuspend each pellet with a total of 20 mL mannitol solution.
Measure particle size using Zetasizer.
Transfer remaining suspension to suitable vials.
Place vials into the lyophilizer.
Measure concentration of samples using HPLC.
Sonicate nanoART suspension briefly at 20% amplitude for 5 seconds.
Transfer 10 μL of the suspension into 1.5 mL RO water within a microcentrifuge tube.
Vortex the mixture for 10 seconds.
Take a 50 μL sample of the water-nanoART solution and transfer it to a filtration apparatus.
Prime the filtration apparatus with 50 μL 0.2μm filtered distilled water.
Apply vacuum to the apparatus until the entire solution volume has been pulled past the filtration membrane.
Affix the dry membrane to an aluminum pin stub using double stick conductive carbon tape.
Sputter coat the specimen stub with palladium.
Image the specimen stub using a JEOL JSM6300F low voltage, field emission scanning electron microscope.
Take the prepared nanoART suspensions and sonicate them for 10 seconds at 20% amplitude.
Place a microscope slide cover slip on an inverted microscope.
Mix 15 μL of the nanoART suspension with 100 μL of phosphate buffered saline (PBS) by pipetting up and down several times.
Visualize the nanoparticles using a 20x objective.
Obtain human monocytes by leukapheresis from HIV-1 and hepatitis seronegative donors.
Purify the cells by counter-current centrifugal elutriation.
Assess cell purity by immunolabeling with anti-CD68 (clone KP-1) on Wright-stained cytospins.

Culture purified monocytes in DMEM supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated pooled human serum, 1% glutamine, 50 μg/mL gentamicin, 10 μg/mL ciprofloxacin, and 1000 U/mL recombinant human macrophage colony stimulating factor (MCSF).
Culture cells at a concentration of 1x10^6 cells/mL in DMEM with the specified supplements at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2.
Plate 2x10^6 cells per well in 6-well plates for differentiation into macrophages over 7 days.
Mix nanoART with culture media (without MCSF) to achieve a final concentration of 100 μM.
Add 1 mL of the treatment medium containing nanoART to each well.
At the desired time point, remove all treatment medium from cells.
Wash cells three times with 1 mL PBS.
Remove adherent cells from the bottom of the well using a cell lifter and place them into a 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 1000 rcf at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and add 200 μL of 100% methanol to lyse the cells.
Briefly sonicate the pellet with a sonicating probe at 20% amplitude for 2-5 seconds.
Store samples in -80°C until ready to analyze drug content.
At the desired time point, wash cells as described previously.
Fix cells for 15 minutes at room temperature in a solution of 3% glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4).
Further fix cells for 10 minutes with 1% osmium tetroxide in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4).
Remove the fixative and scrape cells in 1 mL PBS.
Centrifuge the fixed cells as previously described.
Add 200 μL of glutaraldehyde fixative solution to the pellet instead of methanol.
Cut the cell pellet into thin sections with a microtome (80 nm thick).
Stain the sections with uranyl acetate and lead citrate.
Observe stained sections using transmission electron microscopy.
Treat cells as described in section 7.1-7.2; however, instead of collecting cells after washing, replace PBS with 2 mL cell culture medium without MCSF and without nanoART.
On indicated days or when the cell culture medium turns yellow, exchange half of the medium.
Collect 1 mL of the cell medium along with replicate cells as described in section 7.2-7.3.
Process cells as described in section 7.3.
Add 150 μL of medium sample to 1 mL of 100% methanol and vortex at full speed for 10 seconds.
Centrifuge the samples at 21,000 rcf for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and transfer it to a new tube.
Evaporate the methanol with a vacuum centrifuge; this can take anywhere from 1 to 4 hours depending on the sample.
Store samples in -80°C until ready for drug analysis.
Take mature MDM from step 6.2 and label the cells using a cell labeling solution such as Vybrant Cell Labeling Solution following the manufacturer's instructions.
Rinse the cells three times using 1 mL of culture medium to remove any excess dye.
Mix nanoART with culture medium as in step 7.1 using fluorescently labeled nanoART.
Add treatment medium with labeled nanoART immediately prior to imaging with a confocal microscope.
Capture an image every 30 seconds for 4 hours using a 60x objective.
On desired days, remove all medium from cultures.
Replace the removed medium with fresh medium containing HIV-1ADA at a multiplicity of infection of 0.01 viral particles/cell.
Incubate the infected cultures for 24 hours.
Remove the viral medium and replace it with fresh virus-free media.
Culture cells for 10 days, exchanging half the medium every other day as necessary to keep cells alive.
Collect 10 μL of medium from each well ten days post-infection.
Place collected samples in a 96-well plate and store at -80°C until analysis.
Mix each 10 μL sample with 10 μL of a solution containing 100 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.9), 300 mM KCl, 10 mM DTT, 0.1% NP-40, and water.
Incubate this mixture for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Add 25 μL of a solution containing 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.9), 150 mM KCl, 5 mM DTT, 15 mM MgCl2, 0.05% NP-40, 10 μg/mL poly(A), 0.250 U/mL oligo d(T)12-18, and 10 μCi/mL 3H-TTP to each well.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 18 hours.
Add 50 μL of ice-cold 10% trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to each well after incubation.
Harvest the wells onto glass fiber filters and assess the filters for 3H-TTP incorporation by β-scintillation spectroscopy.
Wash replicate cells from which retroviral transcriptase medium samples were removed in step 11.3 with PBS three times.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde overnight at 4°C.
Rinse cells three times with PBS the following morning.
Use mouse monoclonal antibodies to HIV-1 p24 (1:10, Dako, Carpinteria, CA) for visualization of HIV infection.
Image cells under bright field using a 40x objective.
Mix 10 μL of RTV-NP solution with 100 μL of PBS on top of a glass cover slip.
Incubate the mixture to allow particles to settle and become visible under bright field microscopy using a 20x objective.
